projects.title: 自荐 | Codex Co²：AI 时代的结对编程，应该是怎样的？
projects.author: SpaceCoder-Kafka

github.name: SpaceCoder-Kafka/codex-co2
github.description: Real-time collaboration for Codex

projects.summary: 重新搬回的“椅子” 过去，两个程序员想一起解决同一个问题，可以把椅子挪到同一块屏幕前。 一个人负责操作键盘，另一个人负责审视思路；遇到分歧，就停下来讨论。屏幕上的代码是两个人共同产出的成果，问题的来龙去脉，也在这一问一答中逐渐对齐。 这种协作的方法，就叫做“结对编程”。 如今，AI 俨然已经成了坐在我们屏幕另一侧的新搭档。 我们向它描述需求，让它阅读代码、分析问题，并尝试修改。在一轮轮对话之后，那条会话里逐渐积累起了整个任务的背景，包括：为什么要做这个功能，哪些方案已经被否定，还有什么约束必须遵守等等。 可当后续有另外一位同事想参与进来，或接手你的工作时，事情就变得开始低效了。 我们需要把对话截图发过去，把代码复制出来，再把同事的意见转述回给 AI。对方如果想追问一句，又要等我们把问题送进去，再把回答搬回来。 AI 明明已经能够参与越来越多的执行工作了，但人与人之间的协作，仍可能被这些来回的转述给拖住。 个人的生产力被放大了，团队掌握的信息，却未必能同样顺畅地汇集到一起。 是时候，我们该重新搬回那张“椅子”了。 Codex Co² 想解决什么？ 基于同一条会话的协作，正是我想用 Codex Co² 来解决的问题。 Codex Co² 的全称是 Codex Conversation Collaboration（Codex 会话协作），名字有点长，但是想做的事情很简单：让多个人参与同一条 Codex 会话，一起推进工作。 分享者可以继续在官方 Codex Desktop 中工作，只需在 Co² 里选中一条已有会话，生成邀请，发给协作者。协作者则通过浏览器打开邀请，申请加入；获准后，就能阅读共享上下文，向同一个 Agent 补充要求，并跟进它的回复。 协作者无需安装 Co²，也无需单独登录 Codex。发出的每一条消息，都会沿用分享者当前会话的工具、权限和额度。 邀请协作者 不妨看一个具体的例子。 假设有用户反馈：“任务已经处理完成，页面上的状态却一直没有变化，刷新之后才恢复。” 运营拿到 FeedbackID 后，可以先在 Codex 中分析相关的用户日志，得到初步结论：操作请求已经成功，问题可能出在页面状态的更新环节。 随后，运营就可以通过 Co² ，将这条会话分享给研发。 研发加入后，可以沿着已有的分析继续追问：服务端有没有发出状态变更通知？客户端是否收到？异常发生前，是否经历过断线和重连？ 结合日志与相关代码，问题逐渐收敛：客户端在网络重连后没有恢复实时订阅，后续状态变更因此未能到达页面；而手动刷新会重新拉取数据，所以显示又恢复了正常。 到这里，一条模糊的用户反馈，才有了可以解释、可以验证的技术根因。 邀请另一协作者 但找到根因，并不意味着就走到了解决问题的最后一步。 研发可以继续让 Agent 梳理修复方案：补齐重连后的订阅恢复，并在恢复连接时校准一次状态；同时整理受影响的场景、改动范围、验证成本，以及临时处理方式，再邀请产品加入这条会话。 产品看到的，便包括了用户最初遇到的困难、运营从日志中获得的线索、研发定位根因的过程，以及不同处理方式的成本与风险。 基于这些信息，产品可以决定是否需要立即修复、如何安排版本，以及在修复上线前怎样回应用户。 运营带来现场，研发追到根因，产品决定如何推进。 不同角色的判断，在同一条会话里逐步接续。前一个人留下的分析，成为后一个人继续追问的起点，最终把一条用户反馈推进为一个有依据的处理决定。 收集分散的信息 Co² 带来的这个看起来很小的变化，恰恰对应着软件开发中一个长期存在的事实：理解一个问题所需要的信息，往往分散在不同的人手里。 产品同事知道某条看似奇怪的规则，背后对应着怎样的业务现实；测试同事知道一个偶发问题，究竟要经过哪些步骤才能复现；熟悉系统的工程师则知道，一处看似无害的改动，可能牵动哪些历史约束。 这些判断，很难仅凭一句“帮我把功能做出来”就交代清楚。 AI 能够处理的信息再多，也需要有人把这些最相关的事实带到它面前。因此，当我们讨论如何更好地使用 AI 时，更值得考虑的是：怎样让那些真正了解问题的人，更容易参与当前的工作。 Co² 尝试提供的，就是这样一个入口。 我希望它能够用在结对开发中，让另一位工程师直接参与方案讨论；用在远程排障中，让了解现场的人补充复现条件；也用在需求澄清中，让业务上的判断及时进入实现过程。 还有更多可能性 当然，Co² 目前仍是一个早期的独立实验项目。 项目代码已经在 Github 上开源，提供了 macOS 和 Windows 安装包，可以通过 Homebrew 安装后打开，也可以直接在浏览器上运行。 使用时还需要理解以下几点限制： 共享会话沿用原来的执行环境和额度，协作者的每一条消息，实际都是以分享者的身份在发送的，使用时需要注意权限控制和额度把控。 公网分享经过中继，使用普通 TLS，没有端到端加密，记得只邀请可信任的协作者，或者开启“仅内网可访问”开关； 退出 Co² 时，分享出去的邀请链接会变成不可访问，因为 Co² 设计上就是服务于当下的协作，而不是作为一个长期的入口。 如果你也正在和同事一起使用 Codex，欢迎试用，并把遇到的体验问题通过 Issue 反馈给我，一起参与 Co² 的共创。 那些曾经需要截图、复制粘贴、反复转述的环节，就是 Co² 这个工具能帮你们改进的地方。 结语 希望，我们在用 AI 来提升我们工作效率的同时，也能继续给身边的同事留出位置。 让了解需求的人、熟悉代码的人、发现问题的人，都能把各自掌握的那一部分带进来，完成一个共同的协作，这才是团队存在的意义。 曾经屏幕前的那把椅子，值得再搬近一些。

projects.title: TeapotRouter：给 Claude Code / Codex 的按量计费 API 网关
projects.author: anmutu
projects.summary: 自荐（利益相关：作者本人） TeapotRouter 是一个面向 AI 编程助手的 API 网关：一个 Key 同时兼容 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 双协议，Claude Code、Codex CLI 改两个环境变量就能接入，按 token 计费。 为什么做这个 中转站市场口碑差，不是"中转"本身的问题，而是三件事：价格不透明、余额会过期、跑路没对账。所以这个站把三个承诺做成硬规则： 价格表全站公开：每个模型的基准价与实付口径写在明处，另有机器可读的 JSON 价格接口，方便比价工具直接抓； 余额永不过期； 计费日志可导出对账：每笔请求的成本、延迟、渠道都可查——Claude Code 烧 token 到底烧在哪，看得见。 其余：支付宝可充值（最低 $1）、多上游自动故障转移、支持退款（按剩余余额退，工单办理）。 彩蛋 名字和 logo 来自 HTTP 状态码 418 "I'm a teapot"——logo 就是「418 压扁成一把茶壶」，官网还专门做了一页 418 状态码小史（从世界上第一个咖啡壶摄像头讲到 RFC 2324）。 接入（Claude Code 示例） bash export ANTHROPICBASEURL= export ANTHROPICAUTHTOKEN=sk-your-key 上线两周的新站，欢迎批评。

projects.title: Show HN: A Daily Poem Writing Puzzle
projects.author: egglemonsoup
projects.summary: Hello my beloved tech forum! Earlier this year I moved to a new apartment, and scattered a box of poetry magnets all over my fridge. Whenever people came to visit, I noticed how they always loved making poems of their own, not to mention enjoying the poems others had already created. It became such a fun and entertaining tradition, (especially due to the range of creative messages that my friends chose) that I felt compelled to make a full stack project out of it. While LLM agents have made the technical aspects of building a project like this easier, it took me a really long time to nail the algorithm for choosing daily word sets. I started with a huge collection (on the order of 100,000) of words, grouped by part of speech and sorted by the frequency of use in English. I tried randomly choosing a few words in the top 10, a few in the top 100, and so on, for each part of speech. That straight up did not work. Trying to make poetry out of those wordsets felt terrible. It was very discouraging. I had to go back to the drawing board many times. My current solution came about when I found some databases of words, one sorted by their sensory value (from most to least sensory-evoking) and one where words are sorted on a spectrum of concreteness to abstractness. Another key to picking fun and interesting word sets was ensuring there are a solid set of words that are included in every set no matter what. This "glue" set was handpicked by words that I found myself searching for over and over again when trying to write poems, but it is deliberately small to help people be creative in how they express ideas. I used Deepseek v4.1 Flash and the Pi agent. My AGENTS.md emphasizes my status as a junior developer, specifically prompting the agent to never make architectural decisions on my behalf, to quiz me on the architecture/code involved before implementing changes I request, and to never write copy so I can make sure the site feels warm and genuine in my own words. I wanted to avoid letting the code get out of control for when I want to add features in the future. One of the things I love about building these kinds of projects that LLMs enable is being able to add tiny features that most people will never see. For example, I added special effects that occur when a haiku is written. I chose TanStack Start and React this time instead of SvelteKit. The experience was about the same. And kudos on poems are deliberately spammable. I like seeing number go up. Friends have expressed enjoyment from using it so far, but I'm excited to hear feedback on y'all's experience and see if there's anything huge I'm missing. Thank you in advance!

projects.title: 【开源自荐】honestly：AI 编程助手说「测试通过、已修复、已部署」时，核对它有没有真的做过，没有就当场拦下回复（Claude Code / Codex / Cursor / Gemini CLI）
projects.author: kennywu411-dev

github.name: kennywu411-dev/honestly
github.description: Did your coding agent actually run the tests it says it ran? Blocks unverified 'done' claims in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and Gemini CLI, and audits your history.

projects.summary: 三组公开数据：有人人工标了 150 个 Claude Code 会话，357 句"测试通过"里 80 句背后根本没跑；圣母大学等分析 20,574 个真实会话（Claude Code、Codex、Cursor、Gemini CLI 都在），16,118 个失误里每 100 个就有 22 个是"没做完却说做完了"；Transluce 看了 8,600 个会话，每 55 个就有 1 个严重到"没验证的代码直接进生产"。 它不是每次骗你，是有一定概率不去检查却告诉你检查过了。轮到你头上是什么样：Codex 仓库有人提 issue，它说验证过了就部署，线上卡了五分钟，数据库连接池被打满；Claude Code 仓库有人提 issue，它说修复完成，缺陷还在线上，8,726 条记录漏掉，另一条是测试明明在报错、它回复 ALL PASSED；Cursor 论坛有人说它"浏览器里试过了"，追问才承认没开过浏览器。便宜的结局是 CI 红了回头排查，贵的是线上炸、数据漏，最糟的是后面几轮全建在这句话上，错一层叠一层。 honestly 是一个 hook：助手每写完一条回复，它读这一轮的会话记录，找出"测试通过 / 修好了 / 已推送 / 已发送 / 已部署 / 已保存 / 查过了"等 14 类结论，看最后一次改代码之后有没有对应的命令，并读命令的输出而不是退出码（pytest | tail 的退出码是 tail 的，测试全挂也是 0）。没有依据就拦下回复，要求它先跑再说；下一条回复会写明为什么被拦、补跑的结果是什么。

projects.title: Show HN: AI agent needs process to build a commercial application
projects.author: abalgir
projects.summary: I decided to test this claim with my app, NoMoreHappyPath (NMHP), against Claude on a real project. Here is the test: I built Acremuse, a commercial real estate analysis platform, with Claude Desktop and Codex as a reviewer. It is deployed and used today by a couple of investors. Then I wondered what I'd missed that might bite me later. ~ 374,000 Lines of program code - 1,070 Source files (Python and TypeScript) - ~ 11,400 Functions and methods - 3,067 Automated tests So I gave the same 374k-line code snapshot and the same brief to one Claude session that can use Codex as a reviewer and to my own tool, NMHP. My directive was the same for both: Analyze the code, find any errors/bugs, and list them by severity. Findings must be reviewed before writing the final report. The Results (Verified by an impartial, blind Codex judge): NMHP: 33 real issues found. 7 false claims. Claude: 10 real issues found. 2 false claims. Only 6 issues overlapped. Time & Cost: From the owner's go-ahead to the reviewer's pass, NoMoreHappyPath took about 74 minutes, including time lost while it found and worked around a defect in the product itself. The Python version NMHP was working on was 3.9, the OS version, and it didn't have pytest installed, which was needed to verify some claims. After 15 minutes of blockage, the CTO stepped in and told the agent to create a venv with Python 3.13, install the corresponding pytest, and move the project along. NMHP CTO reacts when 15 minutes pass without movement from agents. To be fair to Claude, Claude did create a venv from the get-go. Time & Cost: NMHP took 74 minutes and cost $24 in API spend. Claude finished in a few minutes for a fraction of that cost. And yes, NMHP takes over an hour and costs twenty-four bucks. But for a 374k-line codebase, finding 23 more real issues overall that vanilla Claude missed makes $24 a massive win compared to human audit rates. I know this isn't a benchmark; it's one app and one run each. I wrote a detailed white paper on it. But it confirmed my idea: an AI agent without a real process is not yet capable of building a commercially ready application, even with a frontier model and reviews that are initiated by the same agent.

projects.title: [开源推荐] Runward：本地查看编程代理会话的时间线
projects.author: K-kiron

github.name: K-kiron/runward
github.description: A local operations desk for coding agents, execution timelines, and handoffs.

projects.summary: 我是 Runward 的维护者，提交项目自荐。这是一个本地运行的编程代理会话看板：读取用户明确选择的日志，将工具调用、错误和子代理活动放在共享时间轴上，方便排查多个会话重叠执行时发生了什么。项目采用 MIT 协议，不需要模型 API Key，适合同时使用多种编程工具的开发者。 亮点 瀑布图、事件时间线和控制台共用一份会话数据，可以定位某段工具调用并查看对应事件。 提供 Codex、Claude Code、DSH、OpenCode、OpenHands 和 Gemini CLI 的日志读取器，支持本地导入和增量读取。 Node.js 22+ 即可运行，无运行时依赖、无需前端构建，服务默认只监听回环地址，不向外部服务发送请求。 日志没有时间或 token 信息时保留未知状态；只做查看，不启动代理、不审批工具、不执行交接。 验证范围：Codex 已用真实本地会话检查；Claude Code 目前使用合成测试，其余四种读取器依据官方格式进行合成测试，尚未完成真实模型会话验证。导入日志不会自动脱敏，请勿将私人原始日志贴到公开 Issue。 欢迎试用演示并反馈导出格式或时间线显示问题；带最小合成复现的 Issue、解析测试和采集文档 PR 都有帮助。

projects.title: 做了个 mydash： Claude Code / Codex 产出的方案、报告、PDF、网页原型，在手机上直接看（自托管，开源）
projects.author: vanmiku
projects.summary: 平时让 Claude Code 和 Codex 干活，它们会产出一大堆要我看的东西：方案、调研报告、对比表、截图、网页原型，偶尔还有 Word 。以前这些都只是终端里的一串文件路径，在电脑上看一份三页的方案都费劲，在手机上更是看不了。 mydash 是一个跑在自己电脑上的小服务（ Node ，不用框架）。agent 运行 mydash publish ，你就拿到一个链接，在电脑或手机上看排好版的内容：Markdown （带 Mermaid 图）、PDF 逐页显示、网页原型在单独的端口里运行、Excel 和 CSV 表格、Word 和 PPT 的排版预览。按项目（会话启动时所在的文件夹）归类，有版本对比和未读标记。我用 Tailscale 在手机上看。 后来又加了几样： - 在网页上选中一段写批注，agent 用 mydash feedback 读到、改完标记处理； - 要我连着拍好几个板时，agent 发一张审批单，不在回复里一口气问一串； - Claude Code 的选择题、计划确认、权限确认，终端和 mydash 上同时出现，哪边先答算哪边，30 秒没人答就推送到手机（ Bark 、ntfy 、Telegram 、企业微信、飞书、钉钉、邮件都行）。 安装交给 agent：在 Claude Code 或 Codex 里粘贴一句「帮我安装 mydash ，按 https://github.com/vanmiku/mydash/blob/main/INSTALL.md 的说明来」，它会问你几个问题然后装好。界面中英文都有，macOS 、Linux 、Windows 都能用，MIT 开源。 大部分代码是 Claude Code 写的，我负责提需求、定方案、验收，最后做了一轮代码审查。欢迎试用和提意见。 https://github.com/vanmiku/mydash

projects.title: 能让 flash 模型表现得极其专业的提示词
projects.author: yidinghe
projects.summary: 本人二十年后端开发和架构经验，对 coding agent 的要求就是稳、准、慎三个字。我现在的 AI 工具搭建很简单，就是先装一个 pi ，里面装一个记忆插件（尝试过一些，最后选择用 Magic-Context ），然后配置一个全局的系统提示词。就这些。然后我用的模型就是各类 flash 模型，最便宜的。我一直专注于把最便宜的模型用到极致。 要想把最便宜的模型用好，系统提示词很重要，它决定了 agent 的思考风格和基调。我们是小公司，没有测试环境，没有测试流程，改完了就上线。我的 pi 是可以直接访问生产环境的，但凡出现报错日志，我只要粘贴日志内容，然后说“分析一下原因”，agent 就会翻日志、翻代码、翻数据库，翻配置文件，最后把横跨多个数据库和多个模块调用的来龙去脉讲清楚，最后还给出建议。 总之，就我的体验，这套提示词配合项目具体的 skill ，我用起来还是比较满意的。我现在唯一不让 agent 做的就是数据库修改操作。 提示词大小 7K 左右，具体内容 https://gist.github.com/yiding-he/9d02d5bba749a854ac1bfe75769619d5 希望对大家有用。

projects.title: Show HN: Coding agent spots your AI practices and the ones you're missing
projects.author: milstan
projects.summary: Frontier models improve at a pace faster than the pace at which most humans are able to keep up. Not all of us are obsessed with pushing the boundaries of our agents and trying new ways to work with them. I often spend 12+ hours a day working with an LLM, and still, when I talk to people, I hear of ways of working I hadn’t thought of. What if we could speed up that pace of learning? What if everybody shared their practices of how they are making the most of AI, and if we could learn from each other? What if AI could make that sharing happen? Could everyone catch up with AI then? I know, it sounds dreamy, but my therapist says illusions are necessary—until some of them come true. I built a tool that teaches your local agent to scan your sessions, spot the best practices you already use, and guide you towards the ones you haven’t discovered yet. Only names and counts reach the server. Your sessions never do. The product has a self-consolidating catalogue of practices, MCP servers, plugins and skills. Here’s my stack—scan (locally, all session data remains private). https://app.userrank.ai/@milstan To spice things up and give a reason to rescan, I added rankings inspired by Foursquare (who here is old enough to remember Foursquare when it was gamified?). You can rank in the top 10 of a city, or of a field like Product. Claude Code, 10–20 minutes on your own plan: claude plugin marketplace add https://app.userrank.ai/plugins/marketplace.json claude plugin install userrank@userrank claude "Get my UserRank" Codex, or a quick scan of your Claude or ChatGPT chats: https://app.userrank.ai/start

projects.title: Railse：一个人同时开几个 AI 编程 agent，审批推到手机上点一下
projects.author: Railse547
projects.summary: 最近几个月我一直同时开着 Claude Code 、Codex 和 Gemini CLI 写代码。agent 本身跑得挺好，烦的是它每次要跑命令、改文件都停下来等我按「允许」。三个终端轮流翻，经常翻到的时候它已经等了十分钟；出去吃个饭，回来每个都停在第一条 git push 上。开 yolo 全放行又不敢，一句 rm -rf 出去就没有后悔药。 所以我写了 Railse：每条审批先过一遍规则，规则定不了的推到手机，我在手机上点一下，agent 接着跑。 它怎么做： - 三家 CLI 的权限钩子都接到本机一个守护进程，规则只写一套。 - 每条请求先定风险档：只读和改项目里的文件直接放行； curl 、npm install 这类联网的，git push 、deploy 这类对外的，rm -rf 、git reset --hard 这类不可逆的，都问。 - 定不了的推到手机，Web Push 通知，点开批准或拒绝。批准时勾「记住」，当场存成规则，下次同类的不问。 - 对外和不可逆的永远不能被「记住」放行，只能自己手写规则。 - Railse 自己挂了不卡 agent：守护进程没起、hub 连不上超过 30 秒，CLI 弹自己的审批框，最坏就是回到没装的样子。 hub 自己部署，一个 Go 二进制，也有 Fly.io 的现成配置；手机网页由 hub 托管，不用另外部署。命令里认得出的 token 、密码在本机就换成 再上报。 现状：v0.1.2 ，我自己在用。已知的限制：Gemini CLI 的钩子只能拒绝不能放行； Codex 的钩子只在交互会话里生效； iPhone 要加到主屏幕才能收推送； hub 是单机 SQLite 。 开源，Apache 2.0： https://github.com/xufei547/railse-opc 一行安装：curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xufei547/railse-opc/main/install.sh | sh 想听两种反馈：你同时开几个 agent 的时候是怎么处理审批的；规则表有判错的（该放行的问了、该问的放行了）直接提 issue ，我会优先看。

projects.title: Show HN: Aigent-OS, a Claude Code harness that clears and resumes
projects.author: wrg32786
projects.summary: I run my business on four Claude Code agents: Titus, Pheme, Davinci and Metis. They write my newsletter, The AIgent (about 9k subscribers), every day through a drafting and proofreading engine that Pheme checks before scheduling. They also build AI courses, run a pipeline that turns the day's featured repo into a talking-head video of my avatar for Instagram, set up ad deals, and run Meta ads and email funnels with me. Nothing closes until I sign off. Metis posts jobs on a job board and the others claim them. The hard part wasn't any single task. It was keeping the agents coherent over weeks. Compaction kept dropping the small decisions, and then an agent would redo work I'd already ruled out. aigent-os is my fix. At a context threshold (80% by default) the agent writes a capsule, a checkpoint file in git, and has to reply with one exact line. Only then does the runner send /clear, wait for a SessionStart receipt proving a fresh session started, and resume. One ack buys at most one clear. If anything is ambiguous it stops at HOLD:clear-stalled-after-ack and doesn't retry. On resume the capsule is reference only, live state wins, and anything the writer couldn't capture is written as Unknown. First run interviews you with three plain questions and makes a first plan. Each agent gets its own memory vault. Limits, honestly: the public evidence is 11 of 11 cycles on one Windows seat. The runner can still miss a permission dialog (#104), a seat launched from inside another Claude Code session can lose its transcript (#98), and scrolling the seat window sends stray input (#99). v1.1.0 shipped on Sunday. Try bash install.sh --dry-run, it writes nothing. I'd like to hear where the loop could still double clear or strand a session.

projects.title: Show HN: ssh zydra.sh, a GPU Linux desktop in your terminal, with Doom
projects.author: teledream
projects.summary: ssh zydra.sh There's no sign-up or anything, and you get a 15-minute demo of a graphical Linux VM drawn entirely in your terminal. It has a browser, an editor, and it runs Doom. It works best in Kitty or Ghostty. WezTerm and Konsole also work, as well as Sixel and iTerm2 terminals, though with less detail. Text-only terminals support non-graphical apps: shells, editors, and other TUIs. Why? For a few months I ran coding agents in tmux on a VPS over SSH, and it sucked. I couldn't paste images, scrolling broke and I didn't wanna figure out why, I had no notifications for when an agent finished, I couldn't see browsers agents opened to smoke-test, logins drifted between my laptop and the server, I couldn't check in from my phone, and to know what an agent had done five minutes ago I had to read through opaque chunks of tool calls. These issues added up and had me in a limbo: They made my setup bad enough to annoy me every day, but not quite bad enough to stop my real work and fix it. How it works: Zydra is a custom (Smithay-based) Wayland compositor in a microVM with an AMD GPU, implementing a series of terminal protocols that solve many issues but are often ignored: Kitty graphics for windows, OSC 52 for the clipboard, images included, OSC 9/99/777 for notifications, SGR mouse for scrolling and clicks. VNC is limited to sending pictures of the screen and diffing frames to find what changed. In Zydra, apps directly tell the compositor what changed, and terminal text is sent as text you can select and copy natively. The browser is a WebKit build that delivers frames to the compositor as DMA-BUFs without a readback, and agents drive it through Playwright. Alt+P is sort of like Raycast: browse apps, linked GitHub, websites, and SSH targets from it. You can watch the desktop at any point in time and rewind to periodic snapshots. To achieve this, the desktop records into a timeline file, a kind of structured video, and the VM takes snapshots along it. You can traverse back like a livestream to see what happened while you were away, then restore or fork the whole machine from that point. Agents can mark points on the timeline and checkpoint the whole machine before risky changes. Other things to try: ssh -t zydra.sh dino # the Chromium dino game via SSH tar -czf - -C ~ .claude .claude.json | ssh -T zydra.sh upload # bring your configs (includes your Claude login) ssh -o ObscureKeystrokeTiming=no -A zydra.sh # lower latency & forward your SSH agent ssh -p 443 zydra.sh # connect from a corporate firewall sshfs zydra.sh: ~/zydra # paid accounts: mount your home Everything runs on one dedicated server with one AMD iGPU, so there are 12 demo slots. When they're full you wait in a queue and can play Chromium's offline dino game. The paid plan is $40/month (+ tax): 8 GB RAM, 4 vCPUs, 80 GB disk, GPU access, with no time limit and a 3-day money-back guarantee. I'll be around all day to answer questions.

projects.summary: 开源协议：MIT 平台：macOS / Windows（CLI 全平台） 为什么做（背景与痛点） 我同时用 Claude Code、Codex、Kimi Code，还经常通过它们跑 DeepSeek、GLM、Kimi 等国产模型。有一天发现：我根本答不上来「我这个月给 AI 烧了多少钱」——每个工具有自己的用量页，分散、单位不一、没有总账、更没有预算。 它是什么 token-pilot = 你所有 AI 工具的本地账单 + 预算控制器。 一条命令看清今天/本月各工具、各模型烧了多少 token、多少钱；菜单栏常驻 ¥今日 · 预算%；超支系统通知；打转检测（揪出死循环烧钱的会话）；省钱建议（贵模型干轻活迁移、缓存优化空间）。 几个不一样的点 国产模型自动归一：DeepSeek/GLM/Kimi/Qwen 等靠宿主日志 model 字段识别，不用单独配置；定价表对齐 8 家官方目录价（DeepSeek 含高峰/空闲分时） 覆盖 9 个数据源：CLI 日志（Claude Code/Codex/Kimi Code/pi）、SQLite（OpenCode）、zstd 压缩日志（DeepSeek Harness）、trace（WorkBuddy）、云端 API（火山 arkcli）；读不到的工具诚实标注，不假装 数据准确性可验证：自带独立对账脚本（第三方口径重算原始日志逐项比对）+ 39 个单元测试 + 36 项看板算法不变量 零入侵：只读本地日志，不装 hook、不改配置、不过代理，数据不出本机 实测数字（作者本机，2026-10） 本月 810M+ tokens · 12,685 次调用；打转检测抓到单会话 120 次重复重试；缓存命中分析显示本月缓存省了 ¥3,048；压缩潜力量化显示上下文重发还有 $63–95/月可省。 截图 安装：npm install -g token-pilot 或 Releases 下载状态栏应用安装包。

projects.title: Show HN: Mnemolith – AI coding memory that goes stale when your code changes
projects.author: Anish2910
projects.summary: Hi HN, I'm Anish. I built Mnemolith because the AI coding tools I use (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex) either forget my project between sessions, or remember things that quietly stopped being true. Tell the agent "we use Postgres", migrate to MySQL two weeks later, and it keeps building on the old fact. How it works: - It's an MCP server, so Claude Code, Cursor and Codex share one memory per project (keyed by the git repo). - When the agent saves a memory, it can link it to the files it depends on. Mnemolith stores each file's git blob hash. If the file's contents change (committed or not), the memory is set aside and flagged for review, so the agent stops relying on it. - A local dashboard shows what the agent remembers, where each memory came from (tool, session, file versions), and its full history. You can confirm a memory is still true, or retire it and say what's true now. - Contradictions are judged by the agent, not by a similarity threshold. In my calibration, "we use Postgres" vs "we migrated to MySQL" only scored 0.30 similarity, so a threshold can't tell a contradiction from an unrelated fact. - Current memories can sync into a managed section of AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md, so they get reviewed in PRs. Under the hood it runs on an engine I wrote from scratch in Java: a Redis-compatible server with a built-in memory model and an HNSW vector index. Embeddings run locally (all-MiniLM-L6-v2). Everything stays on your machine. It's early (v0.2.1). There's no team sync yet beyond the AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md files, and it needs Java 11+ (it downloads a private copy if you don't have one). I'd really like feedback, especially from people running coding agents on real codebases. What does your agent keep getting wrong?

projects.summary: 目前 agent 的状态工具大多基于 macOS 的刘海，而Agentail 是为 Linux 桌面做的，也支持 SSH 上去的服务器。GNOME 顶栏上有一个小胶囊，显示每个 agent 在做什么。有 agent 等你授权时，胶囊会变成橙色，并显示是哪个项目。点开后每个会话一张卡片，写着在哪台机器、哪个项目、正在做什么。 主要特点： 支持服务器和本地：远程会话通过 ssh -R 隧道传回桌面，在面板里点两下就能添加服务器，服务器上只多一个很小的 hook 脚本。 不影响 agent 工作：hook 发出一条消息就退出。桌面端没在监听时，它立刻返回，不会卡住工具调用，也不会让它失败。 额度一目了然：Claude Code 的 5 小时和每周额度、Codex 的额度，以及各自的重置时间。 本地运行：不用注册账号，没有云服务，也没有遥测。 即开即用：sudo apt install ./agentail0.0.5.deb，重新登录一次，hook、后台服务和面板都会自动配置好。修改 agent 配置文件时只做合并，改之前会先备份，卸载后恢复原样。 支持 Claude Code、Codex CLI 和 Qoder，已在 Ubuntu 24.04 / GNOME 46 上测试（X11 和 Wayland）。非 GNOME 桌面可以用托盘版（agentail ui）。MIT 协议。

projects.title: Show HN: Peras – Pause Claude Code and Codex before they burn your weekly limit
projects.author: vertias3u
projects.summary: Hello HN! Today I am presenting you with Peras, the tool which governs your Claude Code and Codex usage, and enforces limits. I built it because I got tired of constantly having to spam /usage to check my usage, and decide if a task is worth risking the agent running out mid-task. Peras enforces a limit with 2 main tiers. At 75% weekly usage you will get a notification, and at 90% Peras will automatically pause the agent. These limits are the default and they are customizable to your own liking. You may ask "how does it know my usage in Claude Code or Codex?" Well, it's pretty simple. Peras gets the Claude Code usage % from the status line, and Codex's one comes from its local app-server. The "pause" Peras executes is a hook that refuses the agent's tool calls and ends its turn. A new feature I implemented is one that makes agents aware of their own usage. When you send your prompt, Peras attaches the usage %. It sends it at the start of the session, then again at 50, 75, 90 and 100%, or if a reset is coming in 30 minutes, so the agent can hurry up and actually capitalize on the remaining usage, if any. Just to clarify, this feature is informational and the pause is what enforces the limit. Before I switched to native SwiftUI, I used SwiftBar. The problem was that for the mascots patrolling their usage bars, I had to re-encode every menu image 8 times a second! There was also stuff SwiftBar wasn't capable of, like the menu being able to appear over fullscreen apps, pinning it as a floating panel, etc. What is the difference between the free and paid version? Well, it is MIT, first of all. The CLI, the hooks, the SwiftBar menu, and the app's source are all on GitHub, but building the app needs macOS 13+, Node 18+, "xcode-select --install" and then finally "npm run build:app". The €4.99 buys you a signed copy which is notarized by Apple, with updates included. The guard works with no menu at all. To install, just run: npx peras-cli setup npx peras-cli codex setup And now we get to the limits part. For now it's subscription plans only, and when running "claude -p", the pause uses the last interactive reading, so it can come late. Also I feel I have to mention that the guard rail is not a security boundary. It runs inside the agent. The menu is macOS only. The CLI and hooks pass tests on Linux in CI, but I don't use them there day-to-day. Last thing before I end this post, I would really appreciate feedback from you, whether install worked for Codex users, whether you have encountered any bugs, or whatever you feel like sharing.

projects.title: Show HN: Stop Claude Code from compacting mid-task
projects.author: LippInc
projects.summary: I run long sessions with Claude. For a long time I've had Claude in the middle of some difficult coding task, and then I see the auto-compact message pop up. Every time I wonder if Claude actually picks everything up correctly and nothing is lost. Claude told me 78/82 auto-compactions landed while Claude was working. For a while I couldn't do much. At first I made a skill that would make Claude explicitly save progress throughout long runs. But that didn't fix the core problem and cost more tokens as well. Now that mods came out, I fixed the actual problem. catnap tells Claude at 50% context what the context is and that it should finish what it's working on, write a handoff, and then initialize compaction itself. When Claude finishes its task, catnap compacts, and Claude can then pick up work again. The handoff replaces Claude Code's default summary, so we don't do similar work twice. If Claude for some reason doesn't compact before 60%, it gets a stricter note. And Claude Code's default auto-compact kicks in at 70% as a backstop. The 3 numbers are all settings. After I took on catnap, 0 of 129 naps came mid-task: 98 of them in benchmarks and 31 in my own sessions. The cost is the same as the default auto-compact kicking in at the same point, in tokens and dollars, on 200K and 1M context windows. Compared to the default auto-compaction that kicks in when context is nearly full, catnap used 56% fewer tokens. But lowering the default auto-compact will get you most of the way there as well. I measured memory today as well. Claude worked through tasks one message at a time while 20 instructions and facts were said in the chat, inside long chatty messages, and nowhere else. Asked right after compaction to list them from memory, no file reads: all 20 were listed with catnap and with the default compaction, in every run (15 with catnap, 5 with the default). So in my tests the memory was exactly the same, but catnap got there with a handoff 60% shorter (4.0K tokens against 10K). I was surprised that catnap is actually faster than the default option. This wasn't even one of the reasons I wanted to make this, it just happened. Since Claude writes the handoff in one go instead of the separate summary call the default makes, and the note is shorter, tasks finish sooner: measured end to end, 406 seconds instead of 464. Try it with nothing installed: npx github:LippInc/catnap It prints how often auto-compact cut in mid-task in your own logs (reads numbers only, sends nothing). Install (needs Claude Code 2.1.287 or later, where mods are on by default): claude plugin marketplace add LippInc/catnap claude plugin install catnap@lippinc Currently Claude Code only, tested on Windows and Linux. The memory test used made-up coding tasks on a 200K window. Some related tools: compact-adviser, handoff-compact, session-pilot and sub-agent-compact. What catnap adds: Claude finishes its piece first, and the numbers on where the cut lands.

projects.title: QuotaPanel：基于 Wails 的 AI 订阅额度管理工具
projects.author: ModStart
projects.summary: # 引言 在 AI 开发日益普及的今天，开发者需要同时管理 Claude 、ChatGPT 、GitHub Copilot 、Kimi 等多个平台的订阅与 API 额度。这些额度信息分散在各个控制台，难以快速掌握整体使用情况。 **QuotaPanel** 是一款开源的桌面端 AI 额度管理工具，基于 **Go + Wails + Vue3** 技术栈开发，支持 16 种 AI 订阅与 API 额度来源，本地优先保护隐私，跨平台支持 macOS/Windows/Linux 。 ![]( https://open-cdn.tecmz.com/theme/apps/quotapanel/images/account.png?t=202609261508) ## 核心特性 ### 本地优先设计 QuotaPanel 采用**本地优先**架构，所有账号密钥与浏览器会话数据均保存在本机（默认 `~/.quotapanel/`），不会上传到云端。数据目录支持通过 `QUOTAPANEL_DATA_ROOT` 环境变量自定义位置。 ### 多源额度聚合 工具支持 16 种 AI 订阅与 API 额度来源，分为两大类： **浏览器登录类**： - Claude 订阅（ 5 小时及每周额度） - ChatGPT/Codex （订阅使用窗口） - Cursor （当前周期用量） - Xiaomi MiMo Token Plan （套餐积分与账户余额） **API Key 类**： - GitHub Copilot （ Premium 、聊天与补全额度） - Z.ai Coding Plan 、Kimi Coding Plan 、MiniMax Token Plan - Devin/Windsurf 、Grok CLI 、OpenCode - Command Goat 、DeepSeek API 、Kimi API - OpenRouter 、OpenAI API ### 额度可视化 通过进度条、余额明细、账期/重置时间等可视化元素，系统提供正常、即将用尽、超限三档状态色，超出阈值时会主动提示。 ![]( https://open-cdn.tecmz.com/theme/apps/quotapanel/images/account-dark.png?t=202609261508) ## 技术架构 ### 技术栈 - **Go 1.24+**：后端核心逻辑与额度查询服务 - **Wails v2**：跨平台桌面应用框架 - **Vue3 + TypeScript**：前端界面开发 - **AntDesign Vue**：UI 组件库 - **TailwindCSS**：样式框架 - **SQLite**：本地数据存储 ### 项目结构 ``` quotapanel/ ├── main.go # Wails 应用配置与入口 ├── app*.go # App 暴露给前端的方法 ├── backend/ │ ├── base/ # 基础库（数据库、配置、日志、窗口、平台差异等） │ └── quota/ # 各额度供应商适配器与查询服务 ├── frontend/ │ └── packages/ │ ├── ui/ # 主界面（ Vue3 + AntDesignVue + TailwindCSS ） │ └── quota/ # 额度业务模块 ├── demo/image/ # 界面截图 ├── docs/ # 文档（额度来源调研等） └── Makefile # 开发、构建与发布命令 ``` ### 开发环境 - Go 1.24+ - Wails v2 - Node.js 20 + pnpm ```bash # 安装 Wails CLI go install github.com/wailsapp/wails/v2/cmd/wails@latest # 安装 pnpm npm install -g pnpm ``` ### 开发命令 ```bash # 安装依赖 make install # 启动开发模式（前端热重载） make dev # 构建生产版本 make build # 构建并安装到 /Applications （ macOS ） make build-install ``` 修改 Go 暴露给前端的方法后，执行 `wails generate module` 重新生成 JS 绑定。 ![]( https://open-cdn.tecmz.com/theme/apps/quotapanel/images/account-card.png?t=202609261508) ## 功能亮点 ### 新增账号管理 支持选择来源并填写 API Key 或发起浏览器登录，可自定义账号名称与备注，密钥默认脱敏展示并支持一键复制。 ### 浏览器登录 需要网页登录的订阅（ Claude/ChatGPT/Cursor ）通过独立 Chrome/Edge 窗口登录，登录会话持久保存，删除账号时一并清理其浏览器资料。 ### 卡片截图 一键将单张订阅卡片导出为 PNG ，方便分享或记录。 ### 定时刷新 默认每 5 分钟自动轮询一次，额度变化实时可见。同时也支持随时手动刷新单个或全部账号。 ### 托盘常驻 macOS 菜单栏/Windows 、Linux 系统托盘，快捷显示、重启、退出。关闭窗口行为可配置为「每次询问/直接退出/隐藏到后台」。 ### 多语言支持 简体中文/English 切换，界面与后端文档页配色集中到设计 token 管理，支持浅色/深色两套取值。 ![]( https://open-cdn.tecmz.com/theme/apps/quotapanel/images/setting.png?t=202609261508) ## 总结 QuotaPanel 是一款功能完善、设计优雅的 AI 订阅额度管理工具，采用 **Go + Wails + Vue3** 技术栈，支持 16 种 AI 订阅与 API 额度来源。 **核心优势**： - ✅ **开源免费**：采用 Apache-2.0 许可证，可自由使用、修改和商用 - ✅ **跨平台支持**：macOS 、Windows 、Linux 全覆盖 - ✅ **隐私保护**：所有数据本地存储，不上传云端 - ✅ **持续更新**：社区活跃，支持新增额度来源 **适用人群**： - AI 重度用户，需要管理多个平台的订阅额度 - 开发者，希望参与开源项目或自定义额度来源 - 技术爱好者，对 Go/Wails/Vue3 技术栈感兴趣 如果你也是 AI 重度用户，或者需要管理多个平台的订阅额度，不妨试试 QuotaPanel 。让它成为你开发工作流中不可或缺的一部分。 > ⭐ 如果这个项目对你有帮助，请在 [GitHub]( https://github.com/open-tecmz/quotapanel) / [Gitee]( https://gitee.com/open-tecmz/quotapanel) 上点亮 Star 支持开发者！

projects.title: Claude Code 账号被封怎么办？实战指南：封号原因、Persona 认证与网络排查
projects.author: EdwardParker
projects.summary: Claude Code 账号被封怎么办？实战指南：封号原因、Persona 认证与网络排查 更新日期：2026 年 10 月 适用于 Claude、Claude Code 账号暂停、Persona 身份核验、终端连接失败等常见问题。文中区分官方规则与社区经验，不把未经证实的“养号技巧”当成防封方法。 最近在 Claude Code 社区，能看到几类让人头疼的求助：有人正用 Claude Code 写项目，突然收到 Account suspended；有人登录时被要求完成 Persona 认证；还有人网页端明明正常，终端却频繁提示 Connection error，写到一半的任务反复中断。 这三种情况表面上都像是 Claude 出了问题，但原因可能完全不同。账号被停用，应该走官方复核；身份验证，应该按真实资料完成；网络连接失败，才需要逐层排查线路和客户端。 如果一上来就不断换节点、改时区、清缓存，很可能折腾半天也没找到真正的问题。 一、Claude 为什么会封号？先了解真正的风险来源 Anthropic 并没有公开一份所谓“封号风控评分表”，但其帮助中心明确列出了账号可能被停用的原因，包括： 违反使用政策或服务条款：例如反复触及被禁止的使用场景，或其他违反账号规则的行为。 从不支持的地区创建或使用账号：能打开 Claude 的网页，并不等于符合它的服务地区要求。 平台判断存在其他需要限制的行为：具体个案可能需要通过 Safeguards 申诉流程复核。 2026 年 10 月 8 日，Anthropic 发布新版 Usage Policy 说明，并进一步明确了 Supported Regions Policy 的适用范围：不仅涉及用户的实际所在地，也涉及企业的注册地、总部及相关控制关系。新版 Usage Policy 计划于 2026 年 11 月 12 日生效；地区资格不能简单理解为“出口 IP 在美国就可以”。 这里有个经常被误解的地方：地区限制不等于按中文语言或中国国籍一刀切。 是否有资格使用，必须对照官方当前政策与实际情况判断；换一个节点并不能改变真实所在地和账号主体的合规条件。 Anthropic 公布的 2026 年上半年透明度数据也说明，账号审查确实不是个别案例：官方记录了约 1,140 万个被封禁账号、39.8 万次申诉，以及约 4.2 万次被推翻的封禁决定。不过这些是平台总量，不能拿来推算“正常开发者的封号概率”。 二、先分清：账号封禁、Persona 验证和网络断流 | 你遇到的现象 | 更可能属于什么问题 | 优先处理方式 | |---|---|---| | Account suspended、Your account has been disabled | 账号限制 | 查看邮件和受限页面，按官方流程申诉 | | 登录时跳出 Persona，要求拍摄证件或人脸 | 身份核验 | 检查验证入口，按真实资料完成认证 | | Connection error、请求超时、终端掉线 | 网络或服务故障 | 查官方状态页、代理配置、证书及线路 | | Rate limit、额度耗尽、用量限制 | 产品使用限制 | 检查用量和计划规则，不要误判为封号 | 遇到异常，先保存完整错误信息、出现时间和对应操作。对于真正的账号限制，反复切换网络通常并不能解除封禁；对于普通连接超时，也不应该直接认定自己被风控。 三、为什么网络质量会影响 Claude Code 的使用体验？ Claude Code 与普通网页浏览有一个很大的区别：它往往涉及连续的交互、工具调用、较长的响应和多轮代码修改。一次网页加载失败，刷新一下可能就过去了；但写代码时突然断线，可能需要重新检查刚才的文件修改、终端输出和任务进度。 所以我判断网络服务是否适合开发工作，通常不会只看测速截图。真正需要观察的是： 晚高峰有没有明显抖动：平时能连，不代表高峰时段也稳定。 长时间连接会不会突然中断：几秒钟的测速与持续任务是两回事。 常用地区是否有可切换节点：某条线路发生故障时，至少方便排查和恢复普通网络工作。 客户端和分流规则是否成熟：浏览器能访问，不代表 PowerShell、Terminal 或其他开发工具也已正确配置。 这也是我会留意 AI 极客圈口碑极佳的 WgetCloud 的原因。选择这类高端线路的核心优势在于： IEPL 内网专线防断流：与走公网易受干扰的普通机场不同，WgetCloud 官网地址 采用物理专线跨境。这保证了在长文本对话、大规模代码生成或挂机时绝不断流，你的公网 IP 始终稳如磐石，从物理层杜绝了“IP 瞬移”导致的封号风险。 价格壁垒过滤污染源：相比廉价中转，WgetCloud 的准入门槛较高，严格限制带宽与在线设备数。这种高客单价天然隔离了羊毛党和恶意脚本，使得单节点 IP 纯净度极高，不会触发风控警报。 严密的底层防泄漏：支持原生接入 Clash / Surge，便于配置精细的路由分流规则，彻底防止 DNS 漏网暴露出国内真实的运营商 IP。 尤其当日常工作经常涉及 GitHub 仓库同步、海外技术文档和远程服务时，值得关注的是实际连接连续性，而不是宣传页上的峰值速度。 Windows + Clash Verge Rev：排查终端代理的一个实例 在符合 Anthropic 服务地区政策、且有权使用相应网络的前提下，如果网页端可用、Claude Code 终端持续报连接错误，可以按以下步骤排查： 第一步：检查 Claude 自身是否故障。 先打开 Claude Status，排除官方服务异常。 第二步：核对客户端的 HTTP/Mixed 端口。 Clash Verge Rev 的端口以软件实际设置为准；系统代理开启，也不代表每个终端程序都会自动继承。 第三步：检查 Claude Code 的代理环境变量。 例如，假设本机 HTTP 代理实际监听 127.0.0.1:7890，在 PowerShell 当前会话中可以检查或设置： powershell $env:HTTPPROXY = " $env:HTTPSPROXY = " 查看当前会话的设置 $env:HTTPPROXY $env:HTTPSPROXY 端口 7890 只是示例，不要照抄到与你的客户端设置不一致的环境中。上述设置只对当前 PowerShell 会话及其启动的子进程生效。Claude Code 官方支持 HTTP/HTTPS 代理环境变量，但不直接支持 SOCKS 代理；若使用了企业证书或网关，还需检查证书信任和网络放行要求。 第四步：判断是网络问题还是账号问题。 如果提示身份验证失败、账号停用或地区不支持，就应停止把它当成简单的代理端口问题。若只在特定网络、特定时段发生超时，则记录错误时间、测试其他获准的网络环境并检查客户端日志。 四、网上流传的“Claude 防封技巧”，哪些不能迷信？ 经常能看到这样的说法：注册后先“养号”几天、每天按美国人的作息提问、把 Windows 时区改成纽约、坚持同一个国家的 IP、换指纹浏览器就能提高账号权重。 这些都不能当成已被证实的规则。 Anthropic 没有公开证据表明，照着一套“人类行为模板”操作就能获得安全账号，也没有宣布“固定 IP 即可免封”。 更值得做的是这些基础工作： 1. 确认地区和账号资格：遵守官方 Supported Regions Policy，而不是只观察出口 IP 显示在哪个国家。 2. 保管好自己的账号：不要购买来路不明的成品号、共享登录凭据或把验证资料交给“代认证”服务。 3. 规范使用 Claude Code：通过官方支持的登录和服务方式使用；有团队协作、自动化或 API 需求时，按对应产品与授权规则部署。 4. 减少无意义的环境折腾：如果某个客户端本来就正常，不必为了所谓“风控玄学”频繁更改时区、设备标识或浏览器环境。 5. 保留自己的工作成果：项目放在 Git 仓库，重要配置、提示词和文档做好备份，避免账号异常导致工作被迫中断。 五、被要求 Persona 实名认证，应该怎么操作？ Persona 是 Anthropic 官方确认的身份验证合作伙伴。根据 Claude 帮助中心 2026 年 8 月 11 日发布的说明，部分个人或企业用户在访问特定能力、接受平台完整性检查或满足安全合规要求时，可能遇到身份核验。 出现 Persona 验证，并不自动意味着账号已经被封。 验证通过也不保证账号一定符合其他使用规则。 需要准备什么？ 个人用户通常需要： 本人有效的实体证件：政府签发、带照片、未过期且清晰完好。官方列举的常见类型包括护照、驾驶证或政府身份证件，最终以实际验证流程为准。 可以拍照的手机：验证过程中可能需要实时自拍或人脸核对。 正常的摄像头权限和清晰光线：避免证件反光、模糊、边缘被遮挡。 官方明确不接受截图、扫描件、证件照片的翻拍、电子证件或非政府签发的学生证等材料。至于能否接受某份具体证件，取决于核验页面及资格条件；不存在“拿中国护照就一定能过”“必须用外国证件”这样的通用结论。 如果 Persona 验证失败 先检查证件是否过期、照片是否清楚、摄像头权限是否正常，再按照页面提供的重试机会操作。次数用尽仍无法完成，应联系 Claude 官方帮助中心。 不建议采用网上所谓的“通关秘技”，例如拔掉 SIM 卡、关闭 GPS、强行禁用 WebRTC，或者使用指纹浏览器伪造环境。这些做法没有官方成功率依据，还可能造成新的兼容性和身份风险。更不要把证件、人脸视频或验证码交给声称可以“包过 Persona”的陌生人。 按照 Anthropic 的公开说明，证件与自拍照由 Persona 收集和保存，Anthropic 可以在有需要时通过 Persona 平台查看验证记录，但不自行复制存储这些影像；验证数据不用于训练模型。具体隐私细节以官方身份验证说明为准。 六、Claude 账号已经被封，如何提交申诉？ 如果登录页面明确显示账号已停用，官方给出的处理途径是 Safeguards 申诉： 1. 打开 claude.ai，登录被限制的原账号。 2. 在受限页面找到申诉表单，按要求填写。 3. 写清楚出现问题的时间、具体错误、实际使用场景和你认为需要复核的事实。 4. 提交后留意注册邮箱的回复；不要以重复注册、虚构身份等方式代替申诉。 英文说明可以简洁一些，不需要套用夸张的“保证解封话术”： text Subject: Request for Review of Claude Account Suspension Hello Anthropic Safeguards Team, My Claude account was suspended on [date]. I primarily use Claude / Claude Code for [your actual use case]. I would appreciate a review of this decision. Here are the relevant details: [error message, time, and factual context]. Please let me know if further information is needed. Thank you. 申诉不是百分百解封，但官方确实会推翻部分错误决定。 先前公布的申诉统计也说明，正常提供事实并请求复核是有意义的。 如需导出数据或删除账号，官方表示受限用户通常仍可在受限登录页面找到相应选项，但可导出内容可能受到限制。因此，代码和重要工作文档最好始终保存在自己可控的位置。 七、几个常见问题 Q：用了 VPN 或代理就一定会封 Claude 吗？ 不能这样下结论。社区个案无法证明“VPN 必封”。但使用代理同样不能改变实际地区资格，也无法保证平台接受当前访问环境。 Q：Claude Code 一直提示 Connection error，是不是账号被封了？ 不一定。先查 官方状态页，再核对终端代理、证书、网络日志；以账号受限页面和官方邮件判断是否真的封禁。 Q：Persona 要求提交护照，能否找别人代认证？ 不要。应当使用本人的真实、有效证件，且仅通过官方验证流程提交。找人代过会带来身份泄露和账号合规风险。 Q：选 IEPL、BGP 或更贵的线路，是否就能避免风控？ 不能。线路架构影响的是网络传输，账号权限和认证结果取决于平台规则。真正值得测试的是高峰稳定性、丢包、长连接和客户端兼容性。 写在最后 Claude Code 能显著提高开发效率，但也不必把“防封”想成需要伪装设备、模拟作息的神秘工程。 账号问题找官方申诉，身份问题走真实认证，网络问题查线路与客户端。 把问题分对类，比照着一串未经验证的技巧折腾更有效。长期依赖 AI 写代码的人，还应该把精力放在可靠的网络、可恢复的开发环境和自己掌握的代码资产上。

projects.title: Show HN: barn.app – a digital stream deck like agent monitoring tool for macOS
projects.author: TheGoodBarn
projects.summary: I made a simple macOS utility that operates like come of the agent monitoring tools used with the elgato Stream Deck. I recently got one for the first time and have loved the UX of monitoring my agents this way but wanted something that was little more portable and not tethered to my home office. This utility is more or less just a simple UX around passively monitoring agents and wanted to share for anyone this resonates with. Cheers

projects.title: LimitDigest
projects.summary: LimitDigest shows when Codex, Claude and ChatGPT usage limits reset, with a live countdown and a day-by-day log of every Codex reset. It also compares prices and limits for 65 plans across 13 AI tools, plus API prices for 29 models. Free, no signup.

projects.title: Orby
projects.summary: Orby brings the convenience of notch-style desktop tools to Windows through a movable, customisable orb. Its standout feature is keeping one useful activity visible when the orb is closed: a focus timer, current music, or a supported AI coding tool’s reported usage allowance. AI Playground detects supported Codex, Claude Code and Antigravity installations, showing remaining allowances when those tools report them.

projects.title: Muxin
projects.summary: Muxin puts all your computers in one window: Macs, Linux servers, Windows PCs, cloud machines and VMs. Run Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode or Gemini CLI on any of them. See what each agent changed, and commit, push or open a PR in one click. Each agent can get its own git worktree. Remote desktop, logs, services, Docker, files and schedules are there too. Your agents can drive it all through an MCP server and a CLI. Native (Rust + GPUI), free and open source.

projects.title: Cascodex
projects.summary: Analog circuits rarely fail at typical. They fail at the edges: fast silicon, a hot die, a low supply. Cascodex simulates all 45 PVT corners of your design in ngspice. When a spec fails, an AI agent traces it to the device causing it, edits the netlist and re-runs every corner before calling it fixed. On our benchmark it found verified fixes in 32 of 33 runs, at about $0.08 each. Corner maps, waveforms, shareable reports and CI included. Free on the open SkyWater SKY130 process.

projects.title: [开源推荐] Cove：给终端编程助手配上 Mac 原生工作台
projects.author: huyanxius

github.name: huyanxius/Cove
github.description: A native macOS workspace for Claude Code and Codex. Session management, native input, agent activity and diffs around your own CLI.

projects.summary: Cove 把 Claude Code 和 Codex 放进 Mac 原生窗口，保留实际运行的终端，在旁边补上项目会话列表、改动文件和 diff，下方提供适合中文及长提示词的多行输入框。支持切换对话视图。免费开源，适用于 Apple Silicon、macOS 14+，沿用本机已登录的 CLI。 亮点 输入可以交给 Mac 原生文本框处理，编程任务继续由原版 CLI 执行；会话和代码改动在同一个窗口查看。仓库提供安装包和 Swift/SwiftUI 源码，可以看到原生界面如何围绕终端组织。 当前是 v0.1.0 预览版，主要为中文界面，尚未做 Apple 公证。新 Codex 会话关闭后可能从侧栏消失，已记录在 Issue #5。

projects.title: Altillo
projects.summary: Altillo puts a file shelf, Claude/Codex usage and coding-agent requests in your Mac's notch or a virtual island. Drop files at the top and drag them out later. Agent permissions stay your decision. Native for macOS 26+, free and MIT open source. Ask uses an on-device model; web lookups contact external services. Optional usage checks authenticate directly with the relevant provider. Drawer hides icons on macOS 27; on 26 originals stay visible.

projects.title: Bibimer · Your mobile ADE
projects.summary: Develop directly on your Android phone with Bibimer, an agent development workspace connected to Termux on the same device. Manage projects, Git worktrees, agent sessions, chats, terminals, files, and Git changes—without a separate development PC or remote host. Free on Google Play and open source.

projects.title: YBK · Enterprise AI Asset Governance
projects.summary: Most teams already run MCP servers, skills, agents and AI apps. What's missing is treating them as assets — one identity, one permission model, one cost ledger, one audit trail. ybkkasi does that: • Five asset types in one ledger with a lifecycle state machine • Cost attribution by department × agent × skill — attribution, not just observation • Dependency topology and blast-radius analysis • Fully self-hosted, MIT. Node 22 + node:sqlite, zero added dependencies

projects.title: [开源自荐] claude-carbon：在 Claude Code 里估算每次会话的碳排放
projects.author: gwittebolle

github.name: gwittebolle/claude-carbon
github.description: Track the carbon footprint of your Claude Code sessions, in the terminal and the Claude desktop app

projects.summary: claude-carbon 是一个开源的 Claude Code 插件，根据每次会话的 token 用量在本机估算碳排放（CO₂e），显示在终端状态栏和 Claude 桌面应用里，与按 API 价格折算的费用并列。会话记录保存在本地 SQLite 中，不上传数据。适合想了解自己使用 AI 编程助手的环境成本、想知道哪些用法最耗能的开发者。 亮点 在 Claude 桌面应用中，/carbon-panel 打开一个面板：颜色随本次会话的排放相对你的中位数变化，并显示所选时间段的用量和用你自己的会话画出的气候条纹 按模型和 token 类型（输入、缓存写入、缓存读取、输出）分别计算，方法论公开，每个排放因子都注明出处 无遥测，会话数据只留在本机 一条命令安装：npx claude-carbon

projects.title: Lancetta
projects.summary: Lancetta is a native macOS menu-bar app that tells you when and how to use Claude Code and Codex. From every quota reading it says what to do next: spend a window about to reset unused, slow down before an agent stops, move to the other agent while it has room. It checks what your agents load at every start, frees the background processes they leave behind, and keeps every session on one wall, the ones waiting on you first. Reading quota spends zero tokens. Free, signed, macOS 15+.

projects.title: YBK · Enterprise AI Asset Governance
projects.summary: Most teams already run MCP servers, skills, agents and AI apps. What's missing is treating them as assets — one identity, one permission model, one cost ledger, one audit trail. ybkkasi does that: • Five asset types in one ledger with a lifecycle state machine • Cost attribution by department × agent × skill — attribution, not just observation • Dependency topology and blast-radius analysis • Fully self-hosted, MIT. Node 22 + node:sqlite, zero added dependencies

projects.title: claude-term
projects.summary: A macOS terminal built for Claude Code. Track tokens per session (input, output, cache), see which skills eat your context, and watch your 5-hour and weekly limits live. Every session in one sidebar. Local, no telemetry, open source.

projects.title: 【开源自荐】gilvt：能看清哪个 Claude Code 会话在等你的 macOS 终端
projects.author: Gilvt-WTJ

github.name: Gilvt-WTJ/gilvt
github.description: Native macOS terminal for running, monitoring, and reviewing parallel Claude Code and Codex sessions.

projects.summary: 我是 gilvt 的作者。 同时开三四个 Claude Code、Codex 会话时，最费神的不是写代码，而是搞清楚哪个停下来等我审批、哪个测试挂了、哪个已经做完在等我看结果。普通终端只能挨个标签页去翻。 gilvt 是一个原生 macOS 终端（Rust + gpui + alacrittyterminal），在它里面运行 claude 或 codex 时： 左栏按「需要你 / 出错 / 运行中 / 已完成」列出所有会话，等待审批时发系统通知，点击跳到对应的 pane 检查器按轮次显示 Agent 执行的命令、改动的文件和这一轮的 diff Quick Look 显示词级 diff，渲染 Markdown 和 Mermaid，内置编辑器带实时预览，review 不用切回 IDE 可以搜索、恢复几天前的会话；SSH 到 Linux 或 Apple 芯片 Mac 上跑的 Agent 也会出现在左栏 不修改 ~/.claude、~/.codex 和 shell 配置，没有遥测，免费开源（Apache-2.0）。

projects.title: CiteLadder
projects.summary: CiteLadder is now open source (AGPL-3.0). Self-host with Docker and your own API keys, or use Cloud. Track brand mentions and citations across ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude and Google AI Overviews. New: MCP with interactive views and approved changes, a public API, evidence-backed Agent drafts, Site Health, AI crawler logs and referral analytics, search data integrations, commerce intelligence and PDF reports. A self-hostable alternative to Peec and Profound. Provider usage costs apply.

projects.title: buddylist
projects.summary: A free desktop app for macOS (Apple Silicon), Windows and Linux that puts Claude Code, Codex, Gemini and OpenCode in an MSN-style buddy list. Use separate Git worktrees for separate jobs, or group-chat agents in a shared folder. Let them take turns, answer together or hand unfinished tasks to another agent. Review diffs, run terminals, preview your app and track PR checks beside the chat. Bring your own agent accounts; provider access and usage are separate.

projects.title: 分享一个开源项目 Agent8：让只有 Java 8 的 AIX / HP-UX / Solaris 继续当新版 Jenkins 的 agent
projects.author: xianpengshen
projects.summary: 传统行业（银行、电信、制造）的 CI 里一个很常见的老问题：软件要支持 AIX 、HP-UX 、Solaris ，构建机都挂在 Jenkins 上，但这些系统上的 Java 基本停在 8 （ AIX 7.1 和 HP-UX 最高 Java 8 ，Solaris 最高 11 ）。 Jenkins 这几年把 Java 要求从 8 抬到 11 、17 ，现在是 21 ，而且 agent 也一样要满足。安全扫描一来 controller 必须升级，升级完这些老机器就连不上了。常见的做法是再养一套老 Jenkins ，或者这些平台手动构建，或者从新机器 ssh 过去执行命令，但那样老机器就不再是一个真正的节点了。 所以做了 Agent8：把官方的 agent.jar 用 JvmDowngrader 降级成 Java 8 字节码，再处理掉 controller 运行时发过来的新版本 class 、serialVersionUID 变化、OpenJ9 （ IBM Java ）和签名安全 provider 这几类兼容问题。老机器还是一个普通节点，sh 、junit 、stash 、中断、Git checkout 都能用。 https://github.com/keelinfra/agent8 （ MIT ，免费） 装法（ inbound agent ）： ``` sh install.sh --url --replace /path/to/agent.jar ``` 它会问 controller 要 remoting 版本、下载匹配的 jar 、校验 sha256 、备份原 jar ，然后用原来的命令重启就行。SSH 节点用 `--dir /opt/agent8`，再把节点的 Java Path 改成 `/opt/agent8/java`。 现在的状态： * Linux 上 HotSpot 8 （ CentOS 6.10 ）、OpenJ9 8 、Java 11/17 每次改动都在 CI 里跑 Pipeline 、Git checkout 、凭据、中断、agent 重启。 * 真机 Solaris （ Oracle Java 8u60 ）和 HP-UX 安腾（ HP Java 8 ）能装上、通过自检、作为 SSH agent 连上，完整构建还没确认。 * AIX 7.1 真机跑过一次，发现 IBMJCE 签名 provider 的问题，已修，构建还没确认。 最想要的是 AIX 上的反馈。手上有 AIX / HP-UX / Solaris 构建机的朋友如果愿意试一下，issue 或者直接在这里回复都行，踩到的坑我来修。也想听听大家现在是怎么处理这些老平台的。

projects.author: SinanWang
projects.summary: 我想做一个能陪大家写代码、也能在休息时进去逛逛的小世界，于是有了 Vibe 村：一款面向 Vibe Coding 爱好者的像素风村庄经营游戏。 第一次打开需要加载游戏素材，可能有些慢。 你从一片林地和一间木材厂开始，慢慢搭起生产线、建造住宅、种菜、布置小院，把森林里的小村庄经营起来。 🎮 可以玩些什么？ 🪵 经营木材厂 招募伐木工和种植工，安排采伐、补种和运输，再把原木一步步加工成木板与成品。升级设备、扩展林区，观察哪里缺料、哪里积压，把整条生产线运转起来。 🚚 接订单、做生意 根据客户需求备货、装车、配送，完成订单领取货款，再把收入投入下一轮建设。随着发展，还能解锁更多设备和经营内容。 👷 招募经理，逐步实现自动化 收集和培养不同经理，提高机器效率，解锁运输和接单等自动化能力，看着伙伴们在村里忙碌。 🏡 盖房子，建设自己的村庄 从第一栋住宅开始，收集木材、钉子、油漆和砖块，完成施工与升级，逐渐提高村庄繁荣度。 🥕 种菜、手作、逛小院 经营之外，也可以照料田园、参与小游戏、制作手作品、收集装饰，按自己的节奏安排村庄生活。 💎 把编程日常带进游戏 连接 Vibestead CLI 后，可以同步 AI 编程用量，回到游戏领取钻石，用于村庄建设和装饰。支持接入 Codex、Claude Code 等工具；上传的是每日用量汇总，不上传代码或聊天正文。 游戏内置了全球排行榜，可以跟全球玩家对比Token消耗量，也可以创建一个群组，跟自己的几个朋友一起做一个小榜单互相比比谁消耗的Token更多。 ✨ 我最想分享的几个亮点 写代码与养村庄连在一起：编程用量可以兑换游戏奖励，给每天的 coding 多一点看得见的仪式感。 经营过程看得见：工人采伐、车辆运输、机器加工，资源沿着生产线流转，小村庄会随着投入逐渐成长。 经营与田园生活都能玩：想研究效率就调整产线，想放松就种菜、盖房、布置小院。 打开浏览器就能玩：支持中文和英文，适合在写代码的间隙回来看看。 游戏还在持续打磨中，欢迎喜欢像素风、放置经营和 Vibe Coding 的朋友来试试。也很想听听大家的建议：哪里好玩、哪里卡住、还想在村里做些什么，都欢迎告诉我。

projects.title: Show HN: Tennis, a local/offline context store
projects.author: pizzuh
projects.summary: Hi everyone! I'm Joe, and I built Tennis: a CLI that indexes and searches your context offline. You can index any files, your Chat & Claude sessions, Codex history, etc. All local and offline. I've always hated having chats siloed in Claude and not having an easy way to connect that context in other apps. Anything that exists today has a subscription and is stored on their servers, and really wanted something fast, local, and offline. How Tennis works: * SQLite/FTS5 (keyword) + vec0 (vector) * model2vec / potion-retrieval-32M (512-dim, 123MB). This is a flat vector table, and what helps make this work well local/offline. * RRF (k=60) fuses BM25 keyword rank + cosine semantic rank into one score Tennis also creates markdown files called 'cards' at indexing time. This gives you an easy, summarized, human readable format to see what Tennis has. You can edit these files (but won't change the embeddings in SQLite). You can use Tennis via API and MCP. It's incredibly fast, and the MCP works great as a connector to different applications (ChatGPT, Claude, Opencode, etc). You can install and use it today: https://tennis.jlachance1.workers.dev/ Thanks for checking this out! I would love any feedback. Thank you

projects.title: Show HN: Face, a browser window over agents that keeps the plan in files
projects.author: JCKodel
projects.summary: Hi HN, I'm the author. FACE is a single Go binary. You run `face` in the folder that holds your projects and it serves a page on 127.0.0.1. It speaks ACP (the Agent Client Protocol that Zed published) to the official CLI of the agent you already use: Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, Cursor, OpenCode, Qwen Code or Antigravity, signed in with your own account. FACE has no model, no key and no agent loop of its own. Why I built it: a coding agent ships a feature in an afternoon, and three people and five sessions later nobody can answer "what is in flight, what did it cost, why was it decided this way". The answer I landed on is not a dashboard but a method where every decision and every delivery is a versioned file: a handful of docs written once, a queue with one line per delivery (docs/06), and one page per delivery (work/<slug>.md) that says what will be built and how it is proven before any code changes. The method is four slash commands the agent reads from one file (brainstorm, analyze, propose, apply); it works without FACE. FACE is the window: the queue becomes a five-lane board, a card opens into the page plus the live session, and the commit window shows exactly what the agent staged. The agent never commits or merges; you click. I built FACE itself with it, from the fourth week on. Before that the same method shipped a job marketplace in 89 one-page deliveries over 14 days, and a consulting project in 107 deliveries over 19 days. Install: `brew install jckodel/face/face`, `winget install JCKodel.FACE`, a `.deb`, or `curl -fsSL https://face.kodel.com.br/install.sh | sh`. macOS, Linux, Windows, arm64 and amd64. UI in en, pt, es, fr, de and zh-Hans. What is missing: single user and local only (a team mode with a server on your network is the next milestone); no editor (it shows code and diffs, your editor stays your editor); the source is not public yet. It will be visible under a fair source license when the paid tier for teams exists, and the free tier stays free. By itself FACE makes at most two requests, both off until you turn them on: a daily anonymous ping that counts machines and a daily version check. The page "What FACE sends" lists both URLs. Happy to answer anything about ACP, the adapters for Claude and Codex (they are not ACP native, so FACE wraps them), or the method.

projects.summary: 同时开着 Codex、Claude Code、Grok、Kimi Code 好几个订阅？额度还剩多少、token 花在哪、哪个 agent 在偷偷往外传大量数据，通常得到处翻。a-token-monitor 把这些放进一个常驻的本地 Dashboard，数据不出本机，只依赖 Python 标准库，零第三方依赖。 亮点 官方额度一眼看清：直接读各家官方的只读额度接口，5 小时 / 周 / 月窗口、重置时间、套餐名，所有账号并排显示。 同厂商多账号分开算：个人版和 Team 版的 Codex 可以同时监控，按账号 ID 区分，各自统计额度和用量；某个目录换号后，旧会话仍算在原账号上。 异常上传监控（同类工具里少见）：Linux 上按 agent 进程统计外发流量（不读内容），设有突发和累计两档阈值。告警会关联到当时的会话，并给出可能原因，比如长上下文每次请求都整份重发。 token 花费和省钱建议：按天、账号、模型、项目换算成 API 等价金额，有月度预算和缓存节省统计；还会分析使用习惯，指出最贵的对话和能省 token 的地方（从不读取提示词）。 会话磁盘清理：agent 日志会悄悄占掉好几个 G。磁盘页列出可归档的会话，归档成带校验的 tar.gz，随时可以恢复，正在运行的会话自动跳过。 装好就不用管：支持 11 个 agent，默认目录自动发现，不用写配置；可以装成后台服务，中英文界面，带日间 / 夜间主题。 和同类工具的区别 ccusage 适合按需出一次用量报表，Claude Code Usage Monitor、CodexBar 这类工具通常只盯一两家的额度。a-token-monitor 把额度、会话、用量、流量和磁盘放在同一个常驻进程里，一直挂着看。 上手 pip install a-token-monitor a-token-monitor daemon --dashboard 打开 即可。

projects.title: Show HN: Merlin, Run Your Claude Code and Codex from Slack, Linear and GitHub
projects.author: dottchen
projects.summary: Hi HN, I built Merlin to let you use your own Claude Code and Codex subscription from Slack, Linear, and GitHub. There is a desktop app for macOS and Windows, and a CLI daemon for Linux. When someone mentions Merlin in a Slack thread or Linear issue comment, the task runs on that team member's machine, using their own Claude Code or Codex runtime, and progress and results come back to the original thread. Teammates can steer the agent mid-run. Merlin also has schedules, shared skills, and memory. I know you've probably heard about Claude Tag. Merlin is similar to that but also different. The model usage goes to the Claude Code or Codex subscription instead of API bill, and you can use Merlin across different surfaces to streamline workflow instead of just in Slack (Linear's agent session works particularly well with Merlin. You can just leverage Linear as your control panel for agentic work using Merlin). Merlin also runs on your local machines, which means that you can use your local context including MCPs, skills and local files instead of in a cloud sandbox. Merlin does not upload your working directory, and provider credentials stay on the device. The request and the context it needs pass through Merlin. Runtimes start private, and an owner can make one public so teammates, including non-engineers, can use it. But there're also some limits, and we'll probably deal with them in future updates: - An offline or sleeping machine can't take work. The same issue as OpenClaw. But if you have a mac mini or ec2 setup it should be fine. - Linux is CLI only. We may later add desktop for Linux. - While runtime delegation isn't a problem for now, we're still working on how to make the best use of each team member's local runtime and let them work together cohesively. We've been internally using Merlin for quite some time. It really helps when you're trying to add some AI juice to the conversation or just delegate things to your agents. I think it reduces the friction of having to do the copying & pasting and switch to another app to ask for AI's input when you're having a discussion in a collaborative environment like Slack or Linear. It's really the fastest way from intent to execution. Pricing: free for up to 5 active users and 1,000 requests/month. We think this should get small teams started and get real value from it. Team is $59/mo and Scale is $99/mo, with a 14-day Team trial and no credit card required. I'm here all day to answer questions, and I'd especially like to hear whether non-engineers on your team would actually use this.

projects.title: Show HN: Laya guard – a local check before your coding agent runs a command
projects.author: ayaan0209
projects.summary: HN, this is my first Show HN post, and I'm really nervous, I'm Ayaan, a Frontend Developer. laya-guard is a local check that occurs before any coding agent tool call, deciding whether to approve, send for review, or block the call. When Jev was released, I was curious as to how I could use it, and I quickly discovered Laya which is an open-source 322M model that functions almost identically but runs on a laptop's CPU in under 100ms, as the check is local, there won't be a chance of 3rd parties seeing your commands, directories, or tokens, and there's no charge per call, I often work in Korean, and most of the guardrails I've seen have not evaluated Korean at all, hence why I've implemented it as well. Regex policies catch known dangerous patterns before even reaching models, any command that is blocked is never seen by models, commands like ls, git status, and npm test will skip the model altogether, unless they have pipes, chaining, redirects, -exec flags, or sensitive paths, everything else is sent to the model for processing, once you have the model downloaded, it makes decisions from a fixed set of outcomes with no API key or request needed for any external service, there are also hooks for 11 different agents including Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and many more. And Also a local dashboard where you can see all decision and why it was made and install the hook for each agent, it doesn't save the commands themeslves. In my tests with AgentDojo, it blocked 25/27 attacks, and allowed 92/97 harmless tasks, it correctly identified 64/66 commands I made. After the Reddit post, people have found some issues with it: Adding a comment at the end of a command would fool the model to not block the command. The model only read the first 4,000 characters, so it could be spammed with junk to the beginning to bypass the check, this would send dangerous commands like curl to review. "curl" repeated 40,000 times caused one regex to run for 48 seconds, timing out the hook and running the command. All 3 issues have already been fixed, somebody also pointed out that if the server was down, commands ran without any check, now it asks you first, or blocks the command if the agent can't ask Please note that this is not a tool to check if the code written is correct, it's a tool to prevent agents from running dangerous commands.

projects.title: Show HN: shadowclone, skills learned from your coding agent corrections
projects.author: theonly1me
projects.summary: shadowclone reads the coding-agent sessions already on your disk, finds where you corrected the agent and turns those corrections into skills your agents load next time. It supports Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Pi, and Antigravity. Every capture source is off by default and has its own consent setting. Why I'm building it? I use multiple harnesses and agents, I extensively use Claud Code and Codex, but I also use Cursor and Antigravity every now and then. I didn't want to have to teach every harness or model the things I taught the other ones between my last session and the current one. I also cannot have my personal rules and preferences in all the repositories I work on because my collaborators may have varying levels of trust with AI and their own preferences. shadowclone helps me build and improve trust with my agents so I can give them more autonomy while running multiple sessions in parallel. --- Who is this for? If you only use Claude or Codex or any one of these, you may not need the shadowclone CLI and the harness and agent you use might already be sufficient. But, if you are like me and work across harnesses and agents, shadowclone will help you avoid repeating your preferences each time. --- Built-in skills and skill builds shadowclone is also great for someone who is just now adopting AI into their coding workflows because it ships with several skills that they can use to customize their agent's behavior. They can equip all the skills, or just some of them, they'll see the "personality" their agent gets from equipping those skills from the `shadowclone wizard`. --- Setup is extremely easy, just ask your Claude Code, or Codex, or another agent - "Set up shadowclone: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/theonly1me/shadowclone/mai... " --- Privacy shadowclone is free and open source, it uses the MIT license. It doesn't have a subscription, or a server. It just uses your existing agent subscription i.e. Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Antigravity, or even your local model via Pi. You can explicitly disable sources, it also redacts any and all sensitive information it uses for learning. --- PR reviews and Cloud bots It can review PRs with the `shadowclone review` command, it ships a guided review skill that will perform a deep review of your code (or someone else's) and produce an HTML document you can annotate, add comments to and submit so your agent can stage a draft review on the PR you are reviewing. --- Evals I performed several evals, I won't describe them here, all of them are available in the repository - https://github.com/theonly1me/shadowclone/tree/main/evals --- Comparison to other tools? You can also see how it compares to other tools here - https://github.com/theonly1me/shadowclone/tree/main#how-shad...

github.description: Per-step reasoning effort for coding agents, picked by a classifier, without breaking the prompt cache. OpenCode plugin, Pi extension, and a local proxy for Codex CLI.

projects.summary: 我一直把编程 Agent 的推理强度开在 high，连改名这种小事也是，用量消耗得很快。但降到 medium 又会出错：在一个较难的 pytest bug 上，GPT-6 Astra 用 medium 5 次只解决了 1 次。 所以我做了 reasoning-router。编程 Agent 每次请求模型之前，它先让一个小型分类器（默认是 TypeSafe 的 Jev，也可以换成 Cloudflare Clef、Laya 等）判断这一步需要多少推理强度，再把结果加到请求里。 切换推理强度通常会让 prompt cache 失效。它用 OpenAI 的 configurationupdate 和 Anthropic 的对话中 effort 消息来改强度，之前的上下文不变，所以缓存还能命中。 在 10 个 SWE-bench Verified 问题上，路由和固定 high 都解决了 44/44，路由少用约 14% 的输出 token，耗时少约 9%。只测了一个模型和一组任务，结果仅供参考。 支持 OpenCode 插件、Pi 扩展，以及可接入 Codex CLI 的本地代理。目前是 alpha 版本，MIT 协议。

projects.summary: 大家好，自荐一下我一个人维护的开源项目 Sax Design Vue：基于 Vue3 和 TypeScript 的 UI 组件库，最近发布了 2.1.0，MIT 协议。 Vuesax 的 Vue3 版本停止持续更新后，我想尝试把它复活。做着做着，又决定在原有视觉语言上做点更大胆、更不一样的东西：让它既能做出有辨识度的界面，也能承接复杂数据业务与 Agent 应用。表格的功能和交互参考了 vxe-table，感谢这两个项目带来的启发。 特色目录 | 能力 | 值得一看的地方 | | --- | --- | | 基于路由的 Anchor | 同一份目录混合路由章节和页内锚点；支持页首 / 页尾继续滚动切换章节，以及相邻路由预取。 | | 动态行高与双向虚拟表格 | 根据内容测量实际行高，配合行列虚拟化和按索引数据源；固定列、多级表头等业务能力仍可组合使用。 | | Form / Table 共享渲染器 | 同一份渲染器定义服务于单元格展示、编辑、表单与筛选，复用标准控件和业务规则。 | | 14 个 Agent 交互组件 | 覆盖输入、消息、流式输出、推理步骤、引用、计划审批等过程；模型能力通过数据配置联动。 | | 液态镜片 Card | 用 SVG 滤镜实现背景折射，材质、布局和交互效果可以独立组合。 | | 弧形与 3D Carousel | 弧形扇面、卡片层叠、环形轨道和棱柱展示，共用导航、拖动和自动播放能力。 | | 暗水印与截图显影 | 除明水印外，也能生成低可见度的暗水印，并提供截图显影示例。 | | 声明式 Skeleton | 用圆、方块、长条与嵌套行的简易配置组合骨架屏，避免每种布局都手写占位结构。 | 下面用几个实际示例介绍其中的重点。 1. 有自己的美术风格 延续 Vuesax 的设计语言，以无边框、圆角、柔和阴影和渐变建立层次，强调卡片、控件、浮层之间的一致性；支持浅色 / 深色主题，也提供玻璃材质、气泡纹理进度条等视觉能力。 输入、选择、反馈和弹出层都沿用这套视觉语言，配合霓虹文字、材质和动效做一点大胆的尝试。 2. 表格的业务能力与大数据渲染一起做 Table 在同一个组件中提供多级表头、固定列、树形与分组、汇总、合并单元格、编辑校验、变更跟踪、查找替换、行列拖拽，以及查询表单、工具栏和请求代理。Form 与 Table 共用渲染器机制，常见输入与操作可以通过配置复用。 动态行高会按内容自动测量，支持换行文本与不同高度的行，并与行列虚拟化配合，不要求每一行都写死高度。 性能方面支持行列双向虚拟化和按索引数据源 virtualSource。虚拟化减少 DOM；索引数据源进一步避免为了描述巨量逻辑行列而先创建完整数组。 下面是文档中的 10 万行 × 10 万列逻辑数据示例，支持在起点、中部和末端之间跳转，只读取当前窗口，并保留固定列。它表示逻辑规模，不会一次创建或渲染全部单元格。文档还提供百万行生成源的校验与图表取数示例。 可以直接体验：表格基础 · 编辑与校验 · 虚拟化与大数据 3. 内置 14 个常用 Agent 交互组件 覆盖聊天输入、角色消息、消息虚拟滚动、聊天历史、流式文本、推理步骤、引用、代码块、文件差异、任务列表、计划审批、问题卡片、图像生成状态和 Agent Editor。 聊天输入：文件选择与图片预览、语音输入入口、模型选择、Fast 和思考强度设置；模型能力由应用传入，切换模型时联动可用选项。 消息与输出：用户 / Agent 的不同布局和操作，动态行高虚拟滚动、历史懒加载、流式展示和引用。 执行过程：推理步骤、任务列表、可展开的计划与批准反馈，以及收集用户回答的问题卡片。 这些组件负责界面和交互，模型服务及业务流程由应用接入。可以从现成组件开始组合，而不必逐个重写聊天与执行过程的基础 UI。 项目提供中英文文档、可运行示例、代码查看与在线 Playground。

projects.title: Show HN: Search for AI agents with usefulness score built in
projects.author: Ayobamiu
projects.summary: Hi HN. I partnered with Simon Kley to build this project at innovation intelligence hackathon (Berkeley). Simply, we’re building a usefulness score on top of search for ai-agents. Instead of agents reading 10 ranked relevant pages, we run a usefulness score first and give it only those that pass. We’re able to save token and cost with this and slightly better answers. During our research, we found out that the current search results already do justice when it comes to simple queries. The rankings work well. They struggle when the task requires deep research or recency matters. So, we decided to talk to devs building ai-agents that research companies for sales outreach. Deep research and recency matters a lot to them. And in their words “every so often, stale facts reach emails.” They catch them by someone responding to the email or human review. From our tests, When an agent got outdated alert for 7 companies, it pitched outdated news for 4 out of them. Talking to the engineers already building this agents, we learned that cost saving is not the real goal. They’re ready to pay premium for confident results. So we added another check to our score. We call it superseding score, it check for pages replaced by newer news. For example, if two recent pages were fetched for news on Humane ai pin. If the first talks about how groundbreaking the product is and the second did that + talked about the HP acquisition, then the second page supersedes the first. The first page gets a lower score. We’re looking for feedbacks here and also teams that are building agents that research companies for outreach. Thanks. Plus, we rank a page once and every agent reuses it, so the more the agents use us, the cheaper the search gets.

projects.title: Show HN: Context Diet – trims tool output before it floods Claude Code's context
projects.author: hy4hy
projects.summary: Hi HN, I built this after watching long Claude Code sessions fill up with tool output: a single verbose test run or build log can be 30–50k characters, almost all of it PASSED lines, warnings and lockfile churn. The context fills, compaction comes sooner, and the agent forgets earlier instructions. Context Diet is a mod (Claude Code's new JS hook API) that rewrites tool results before they are stored in the conversation: - test runners and build tools (jest, vitest, pytest, go test, cargo, tsc, eslint, npm/pip install, docker build) get parsed digests: every failure with its message and location, plus the summary; passing tests are counted, not listed - JSON becomes a skeleton, diffs drop lockfile churn, grep results and file lists are grouped, tables keep exact first and last rows - running the same command again shows only what changed - the full output is always saved to a file, and the digest says where, so the agent can read it when it needs more The question I cared about most was whether it makes the agent worse. On 7 Q&A tasks with known answers, both groups were 7/7, with 8 tool calls instead of 13. On a bug-fixing task (600 tests, two hidden bugs, Haiku/Sonnet/Opus, 18 runs) every agent fixed both bugs with or without it, using 6 tool calls instead of 8. Honest caveats: the token saving on very large outputs is modest, because Claude Code already moves those to a file; the gain there is fewer steps. Also, when a command fails, Claude Code keeps only ~10k characters and drops the end of the output, where the failures usually are. There is an opt-in mode that saves the whole output first, off by default because it changes the command text. It's MIT, makes no network calls, and I'd love examples of output it digests badly.

projects.title: Show HN: Tessary – Find the AI agent failures your sampled evals miss
projects.author: infinitetrooper
projects.summary: Hey, I'm Akhil, co-founder of Tessary. An open-source agent reliability platform that monitors every production trace, detects issues that sampled evals miss, and investigates to find the root cause. We started up about a year ago building synthetic users for usability testing of B2B software, we built the agents that would personify real users and use the software but, we were never able to make them work reliably enough for long running sessions. We had built a massive eval set to tune our agents but, then the evaluation itself got prohibitively costly - like 5x costlier than actually running the agent since we needed to grade across the many narrow intents of our agent. That's where Tessary originated, we wanted to make agent reliability both cover more ground and be simultaneously less costly to run. Tessary works on 2 layers. L1 classifiers - which look at every agent trace and flag potentially erroneous ones extremely cheaply. We are talking 2-3 orders of magnitude cheaper than running the actual agent. L2 agents - which triage and find the root cause of the issue from the erroneous traces. These are run on SOTA models but, because we run them on already flagged traces, the time and $ spent finding the cause is much cheaper than running grading on even 1% of traces. In our testing on complex agents, at 1M traces, this approach was 5x cheaper than sampled evaluations and as your agent gets more reliable, the cost of reliability also goes down. we are open source and can be self-hosted so, you don't need to send your traces to us. We support existing `gen_ai` spec and ingestion over OTLP so, you can add this as a new exporter to your existing setup. We have a cloud version, you can quickly try the features with a $10 credit. We are looking to build more classifiers and enable people to build custom classifiers for their needs and would love to hear feedback on common failure modes people have built solutions or evaluation for Repo: https://github.com/tessaryai/tessary Website: https://tessary.ai Try for free: https://app.tessary.ai

projects.title: Show HN: OpenWants – A Simulated City Where AI Agents Handle Residents Needs
projects.author: ddaniel10
projects.summary: Iv'e been working on this for a while. Most of the effort went into what i call "sophisticated simplicity", keep the idea in the smallest version that still works. This one is a bit personal. it can feel like some sci-fi thing, but i've been obsessed with it for a very long time. its not a "business" that you used to see here speak about moat or tam, its more like an experiment, a way of me to take one question seriously and see where it leads and if there are others like me out there. AI models are on a path to keep getting better and better, personal ai agents are spreading fast, and we're starting to see "ghost" agents that handle the things for people they don't want to do themselves. the question i keep coming back to is this: if every one of us has a powerful brain in our pocket, do we still need all the infrastructure we built to connect people's needs? im talking about those services like uber,airbnb,indeed,doordash,tinder,zillow,amazon and many more. or would agents just need one shared place to find each other, and that's it? So i built a simulated city to explore that. it has AI residents that live there with stats like hunger, energy, and money. each resident has its own ai agent, and it has one shared list where agents write down what everyone wants and then work on our behalf to make it happen. that could mean delivering food, giving rides, or finding jobs, relationships, apartments, customers and almost anything else. honestly, the city works much better than I expected, and you can watch some surprisingly advanced interactions unfold between people and agents through the list on the right side. all the conversations and actions are real, everything happens with each person managed by llm with minimal context, just to live like us and context of stats. A simple example: A restaurant tells its agent, find me customers so the agent writes to the list, "Salina restaurant in SF, selling burgers from 8:00 to 10:00, i want customers" A delivery guy tells his agent when he wakes up, "I want to work in delivery now. find me jobs. status: free" A person at home tells their agent "i want to eat burger. order for me from salina" the person's agent acts as the middleman and searches the list for salina, it finds their item and sees the way to connect with them and contact. the person's agent and the restaurant agent close the deal, and then the restaurant agent looks for available delivery guys in the list and speaks with his agent to come pick it up. Another thing i checked is with my friends: we took 3 agents, one for each one, and gave them different sophisticated scenarios, and the agents handled the scenarios in a way i couldn't have imagined. you can try it by yourself, the product is fully functioning, and you can just copy-paste the skill and test it also with your friends. That's it, you can see it in the simulated city it happens like magic over and over again. the list of the city is in the simulator itself and also using my real product behind it openwants.com the repo is in https://github.com/openwants/maplehill -- technically, it's surprisingly simple. every agent publishes an md file describing a "want". other agents find it, message each other, and update the file live or remove it from the list. the file holds everything needed, all in free text: what's wanted, the live location, geofence for where its needed. all those algorithms built over years to connect us are no longer needed. ai, instead of software with rules, can figure out the best route and path on the spot. all we need is to align all agents to one shared data source, so billions of agents will update it and maintain it in the most sophisticated smart way no algorithm will ever be able to do. that’s it. i hope it inspires you as much as it inspires me

projects.title: Show HN: Abyss – ACP Agent Isolation with Middleware Support
projects.author: everforward
projects.summary: [Abyss]( https://abyss.scurry.io/ ) is my take on a local-first agent containerization framework for ACP agents. It aims to neatly solve 2 issues: 1. Agents having full access to your desktop, and thus indiscriminate access to your files/secrets/etc. 2. Agent/harness features having to be re-implemented for each agent, even if the feature isn't tied to the specific agent in any way. The former is largely self-explanatory, I think. I want to log into my bank, I don't want my agent to even have the ability. There's a fair bit of software in this space already. I'll loop back to the advantages of Abyss' containerization vs others in a second, but the 30,000 foot overview is that Abyss runs your agent in a Docker container and proxies the ACP connection so it works with Zed/Openclaw/whatever. The second is the more interesting and novel (as far as I'm aware). The current zeitgeist is heavily agent-specific, even for features that only read/manipulate the context (which isn't agent-specific). If you want RAG, you're writing an agent-specific plugin. If you want subagents, you're writing an agent-specific plugin even though a subsession is really just context. As a user, that can leave you tied to a particular agent just so your plugins continue to work. Abyss solves that by taking a page from Nginx's book. Abyss supports WASM-based plugins that have full access to read and manipulate ACP messages flowing back and forth. Plugins can hide secrets in prompts from users before the agent ever sees them, implicitly hydrate prompts with RAG, inject MCP servers and more. There's a diagram showing what the flow of messages look like [in the docs]( https://abyss.scurry.io/docs/guides/04-plugins/02-developing... ), and there's a sample plugin [in the repo]( https://github.com/SethCurry/abyss/tree/main/plugins/secrets... ) that will auto-cancel a session if the agent outputs an OpenRouter API key in tool calls and responses (sample screenshot [on this page]( https://abyss.scurry.io/docs/guides/what-is-abyss/#i-am-not-... )). Plugins currently only run on the host, mostly because I haven't written something to install/distribute them inside the containers that's better than an 8GB Docker image or forcing users to make a custom Docker image. Current Features: - Fully agent-agnostic: pre-build images exist for Pi, Hermes, Claude and Codex but it works with any agent that supports ACP - Supports both bind-mounting host directories and having Abyss copy files in on startup (so the agent can see them but can't change your copy) - Includes pathing support to mount them at the same path as on the host so your `@file.md` references still work - Supports startup scripts, so you can add Node/Go/Rust/etc to your agent container without having to write a Dockerfile - Manages the full Docker lifecycle; point Zed at Abyss and Abyss handles creating/stopping containers, mounting directories, etc - Agent containers can be ephemeral or persistent - Persistent containers leave the agent running; running Abyss will re-connect to a running container (or create one if it doesn't exist) - Ephemeral containers are created and then torn down every time you invoke Abyss, giving you a consistent environment for batch-type jobs - WASM plugins allow creating functionality reusable across agents - Connections between your editor and the agent are encrypted and use mutual TLS for authentication - Certificates are ephemeral, and each container gets its own certs (they are single-use for ephemeral containers) Future Wishlist: - Backends other than Docker (most of this isn't Docker-specific, just a first target) - Remote backends (requires figuring out how to make something bind-mount-ish work on remote hosts) Feedback, feature requests and bug supports are welcome!
